anya: quick question — are we happy with current benchmark methodology for SLO tradeoffs? replay vs loadgen is giving different p99s :thinking_face:
ben: short answer: no. replay shows clean p95 but loadgen exposes p99 spikes when microbatching fluctuates
frank: replay has realistic KV-cache warmups but it's too 'soft' on tail because it preserves arrival patterns. loadgen gives worst-case bursts we actually see in spikes-on-frontend
sara: can we combine them? e.g., run replay baseline then inject 5s 5x traffic spikes from loadgen every 30s to stress microbatching logic
max: +1. also need to vary prompt length distribution — kernels pick different paths for long vs short seqs. saw kernel fallback to generic GEMM at >1024 which killed tail
anya: exact numbers from last run: replay: p50 28ms, p95 92ms, p99 120ms. loadgen (spikey): p50 35ms, p95 140ms, p99 420ms. KV hit-rate during spike fell from 92% -> 58%
perf-bot: perf summary (run 2026-11-01): kernel-choice mismatch events=34, avg microbatch size=3.6, cold-KV miss windows=12, mean tail-add=+260ms
ben: this smells like batching heuristic + KV eviction interplay. small microbatches in spikes cause more dispatch overhead and miss in shared KV shards
frank: we should instrument per-request path: kernel id, batch_id, kv_hit, queuing_time_ms. minimal schema like: `{req_id,kernel,mb_size,kv_hit,queue_ms,exec_ms}` in logs
sara: agree. also we need consistent p99 measurement epoch (min 5m sustained) — transient 10s spikes shouldn't dominate unless they're expected in prod. what's our SLO? 200ms p99 for low-tier, 500ms p99 for best-effort
max: proposal: new harness: (1) replay with production traces for 10m, (2) 15m mixed phase with 30s 5x spikes from loadgen + varied prompt length, (3) long tail run 30m steady high-rps to capture kernel degradation. record per-request fields and KV heatmap
anya: sounds good. one more: add warm/rollback test for kernel selector on quantized models — some kernels are faster but cause jitter under narrow sequence lengths
ben: can we add automatic regression flagging? if p99 increases >20% or kv-hit drops >15% then fail. also compare sample tails (histograms) rather than single-number percentiles
frank: put a small script in perf infra that diffs histograms and posts to #eng-runtime with a short blurb + link to artifacts
deploy-bot: scheduled run queued: mixedworkload-2026-11-02T02:00Z (owner: eng-runtime) :robot_face:
anya: assigning action items: frank -> logging schema PR, sara -> harness config for mixed spikes, ben -> regression rules, max -> kernel-selector test cases. I'll coordinate follow-up next week :thumbsup:
ben: thanks — I'll start with the regression thresholds and add a dashboard for kv-hit vs p99
anya: great. closing thread.
